skill.name: event-sourcing-architect
skill.description: Expert in event sourcing, CQRS, and event-driven architecture patterns. Masters event store design, projection building, saga orchestration, and eventual consistency patterns. Use PROACTIVELY for event-sourced systems, audit trails, or temporal queries.
skill.summary: Design event-sourced systems with CQRS, event stores, projections, sagas, and versioning.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: No static findings were reported, and review of SKILL.md found no executable code, network access, file access, or prompt injection attempt. The skill is a prompt-only architecture guide for event sourcing and CQRS patterns.

content.value_statement: Event-sourced systems are hard to design because state, history, projections, and workflows must stay coherent. This skill guides architecture decisions for event stores, CQRS models, sagas, and evolution plans.
actual_capabilities: Helps identify aggregate boundaries and event stream design.
Guides immutable event modeling and command handler structure.
Plans CQRS read models and projection rebuild strategies.
Designs saga and process manager workflows across aggregates.
Recommends snapshotting strategies for long-lived aggregates.
Explains event versioning and schema evolution approaches.
limitations: It does not implement code or run event store migrations.
It is not suited for simple CRUD domains.
It assumes teams can operate event stores and projections.
It does not guarantee immediate consistency across all workflows.

use_cases.title: Plan Audit-First Domains
use_cases.description: Design event streams for domains that need full history, traceability, and temporal queries.

use_cases.title: Model Complex Workflows
use_cases.description: Define commands, events, aggregates, and compensating actions for multi-step business processes.

use_cases.title: Scale Read Performance
use_cases.description: Separate write models from optimized projections for reporting, dashboards, and query-heavy workloads.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Fit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner evaluation of whether event sourcing is appropriate.
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess whether event sourcing is appropriate for this domain: [describe domain]. Include benefits, risks, and simpler alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Define Aggregates
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate domain modeling for a new service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me identify aggregate boundaries, command names, event names, and event streams for this workflow: [describe workflow].

prompt_templates.title: Design Projections
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced CQRS planning for read-heavy requirements.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design CQRS projections for these query requirements: [list queries]. Include rebuild strategy, idempotency, and consistency expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Evolution
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced system design for production operations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an event versioning, snapshotting, and saga orchestration plan for this existing event-sourced system: [describe system].

output_examples.input: Design event sourcing for an order fulfillment workflow with payment, inventory, and shipping steps.
output_examples.output: A recommended aggregate split, event list, saga responsibilities, compensating actions, and projection plan for customer and operations views.

output_examples.input: Review whether event sourcing is justified for a small internal CRUD application.
output_examples.output: A fit assessment that explains why CRUD may be simpler, plus conditions that would justify event sourcing later.

output_examples.input: Plan schema evolution for existing events that need a new shipping address format.
output_examples.output: A versioning approach with compatibility rules, projection rebuild guidance, and rollout checks for production safety.

best_practices: Model events as immutable business facts, not implementation messages.
Design idempotent handlers and projection rebuilds before production use.
Define versioning, correlation IDs, and consistency expectations early.
anti_patterns: Do not use event sourcing when basic CRUD meets the domain needs.
Do not mutate or delete committed production events.
Do not hide cross-aggregate workflows inside a single large aggregate.

faq.question: What does this skill help design?
faq.answer: It helps design event stores, aggregates, commands, events, projections, sagas, snapshots, and versioning strategies.

faq.question: Does it write production code?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance and design structure for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code sessions.

faq.question: When should I avoid this skill?
faq.answer: Avoid it when the domain is simple, CRUD is sufficient, or immediate consistency is required everywhere.

faq.question: Can it help with audit trails?
faq.answer: Yes. It is well suited for systems that need complete history, temporal queries, and traceable state changes.

faq.question: Can it help with CQRS projections?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides read model design, projection optimization, rebuild planning, and eventual consistency expectations.

faq.question: Is this skill safe to install?
faq.answer: The reviewed skill is prompt-only and contains no executable code or detected dangerous behavior.
